claims.text: Adding approximately 5 at.% Al to an elemental Cr coating will enable in situ Al2O3 formation during early oxidation.
The resulting Al2O3 will form a continuous, nanometric, and uniformly distributed layer.
The Al2O3 layer will form at the interface between the Cr–Al coating and the zirconium-alloy substrate.
Al in the Cr–Al coating will preferentially oxidize under the specified exposures.
The interfacial alumina layer will act as a stable barrier to Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The alumina barrier will preserve the protective oxidation behavior of Cr.
Suppressing interfacial transport with alumina will reduce coating spallation.
Suppressing interfacial transport with alumina will reduce coating blistering.
The Cr–Al coating will exhibit lower oxide growth rates than an unmodified Cr coating.
The Cr–Al coating will retain better coating integrity than an unmodified Cr coating.
The Cr–Al coating will exhibit less Cr–Zr interfacial diffusion than an unmodified Cr coating.
The proposed Cr–Al coating will improve durability during subcritical-water exposure at approximately 350–400°C for more than 3000 hours.
The proposed Cr–Al coating will improve durability during steam exposure at approximately 1000°C for 30–60 minutes.
The proposed coating will function within simulated reactor water-chemistry and radiation environments.
Unmodified elemental Cr coatings exhibit significant Cr–Zr interdiffusion under accident conditions.
Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of unmodified Cr coatings under accident conditions.
Successful performance depends critically on forming and retaining a uniform alumina barrier throughout both exposure regimes.
